podcast.body: This album was released by Blink-182 almost exactly three years after their drummer, Travis Barker, survived a near-fatal plane crash. The tragic incident, and Barker's survival, is credited with spurring the band's reunion, leading to the creation of this album. "Almost three years to the day after the crash, Blink released an album called Neighborhoods."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, released on September 27, 2011, marked the band's first record together in nine years and nearly three years after Travis Barker's plane crash. Its creation was a long and emotionally challenging process, exacerbated by the members' busy individual schedules, Tom DeLonge's continued work with Angels & Airwaves, Mark Hoppus's TV show commitments, Travis Barker's grief over DJ AM's death, and the absence of their longtime producer Jerry Finn. The album was one of the most anticipated releases of 2011 but sold approximately 500,000 units worldwide, which was considered less than stellar. "They called it neighborhoods, and this was the first single."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released after an eight-year hiatus, this album's performance was met with dissatisfaction by their label. This unhappiness ultimately led to the band being cut loose and forced to go indie in October 2012. "Their label wasn't happy with the performance of Neighborhoods, and in October 2012, the band was cut loose and forced to go indie, a pretty demoralizing thing after selling tens of millions of albums."
